headline: METALSOURCE HITS 1,580 g/t AGEQ OVER 0.64m AT SILVER HILL — 11.8m CORRIDOR AT 245 g/t EXTENDS HIGH-GRADE CORRIDOR 28m SOUTH (CSE:MSM)
snippet: Metalsource Mining Inc. (CSE:MSM) released June 24 additional assay results from the Silver Hill Project's ongoing drill program, with step-out hole SH26-18 returning 11.8 metres grading 245 g/t silver equivalent — including 1.4 metres at 833 g/t AgEq and a bonanza-grade core of 0.64 metres at 1,580 g/t AgEq — while extending the high-grade corridor approximately 28 metres south of previously reported hole SH26-08, confirming that the polymetallic system remains open along strike. The results reinforce the continuity of the Silver Hill corridor, with multiple assays still pending from the current campaign as the company works toward defining the full footprint of this historically producing silver-gold-polymetallic system.

headline: EQUINOX-ORLA $5.1B PROXY MAILED — JULY 22 VOTE WOULD MAKE EQUINOX CANADA'S 2ND-LARGEST GOLD MINER AT 1.1M OZ ANNUAL OUTPUT
snippet: Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX:EQX) announced June 23 it has filed and mailed meeting materials for the July 22 special shareholder vote to approve its all-share acquisition of Orla Mining Ltd. (TSX:ORLA) in a transaction valued at approximately $5.1 billion, under which each Orla share exchanges for 1.00 Equinox share — leaving former Orla holders with approximately 33% of the combined company and existing Equinox holders with 67%. The combined company is expected to produce approximately 1.1 million ounces of gold in 2026 with Canadian mines contributing nearly 700,000 ounces, creating Canada's second-largest gold producer and one of the more compelling North American consolidation stories in a market where gold's correction from $5,589 is compressing junior valuations and increasing M&A firepower for well-capitalised producers.

headline: BEIJING BANS DUAL-USE EXPORTS TO MP MATERIALS AND USA RARE EARTH — CHINA TARGETS TRUMP'S MINE-TO-MAGNET PAIR IN CRITICAL MINERALS WAR
snippet: China's Commerce Ministry added MP Materials — operator of the only active US rare earth mine — and USA Rare Earth to its export control list on June 22 alongside eight other US firms, prohibiting any entity globally from supplying dual-use items originating in China to those companies, an extraterritorial escalation that goes beyond previous license-only requirements. While analysts say the immediate impact is largely symbolic since both firms have minimal direct Chinese input dependence, the move underscores Beijing's willingness to leverage its 90% refining and 95% permanent magnet production dominance as a geopolitical weapon against the Trump administration's $3.5 billion mine-to-magnet buildout — and serves as a reminder that any future tightening of controls on rare earth compounds could become operationally significant for Western defence supply chains.

headline: ALAMOS GOLD DISCOVERS NEW HIGH-GRADE ZONE 300m WEST OF ISLAND GOLD MINE — 5.2m AT 12.05 g/t AU, $43M DISTRICT BUDGET UP 79% FROM 2025
snippet: Alamos Gold Inc. (TSX:AGI) announced June 22 the discovery of a new high-grade zone at its Island Gold District in Ontario, 300 metres along strike to the west of current mineral reserves, intersected in seven holes between 750 and 1,000 metres from surface — with the best result, MX26-031, returning 5.2 metres at 12.05 g/t gold from approximately 968 metres depth, while West Extension hole MX26-035W returned 5.6 metres at 8.07 g/t gold from approximately 928 metres. Alamos simultaneously increased its 2026 district exploration budget to $43 million — up 79% from 2025's $24 million — with over 98,000 metres of underground and surface drilling planned across multiple high-grade targets aimed at adding higher-grade mill feed for the recently expanded Magino processing facility.

headline: FARADAY COPPER ADDS 67m OF NEAR-SURFACE COPPER AT AMERICAN EAGLE — PHASE IV COMPLETE, DRILLING HALTED FOR BHP SAN MANUEL ACQUISITION CLOSE
snippet: Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY) released June 24 results from 18 Phase IV drill holes at its Copper Creek Project in Arizona, confirming near-surface copper mineralisation across the previously underdrilled American Eagle area with best intercepts of 67.0 metres at 0.30% copper from 30 metres depth and 35.35 metres at 0.58% copper from 85.40 metres in shallow-angled step-out holes testing the top 50 metres of surface. The company paused all drilling as of June 20 pending the expected Q3 2026 close of its proposed acquisition of BHP's adjacent San Manuel property — under which BHP receives a 30% equity stake in Faraday — a transaction that would combine both properties into approximately 27,000 contiguous acres and create one of the largest copper district consolidations in Arizona in decades.

headline: KOBO RESOURCES CONFIRMS 97% AVERAGE GOLD RECOVERY AT KOSSOU — CONVENTIONAL CIL VALIDATED AHEAD OF H2 2026 RESOURCE ESTIMATE
snippet: Kobo Resources Inc. (TSXV:KRI) released June 24 metallurgical test results for the Kossou Gold Project in Côte d'Ivoire showing overall gold recoveries of 94% to 99% — averaging approximately 97% — across samples from the Jagger and Road Cut Zones processed by SGS Canada using a conventional gravity and CIL flowsheet, confirming the same processing route used by multiple operating gold mines in the country. With two drill rigs still active across a 222-hole, 42,000+ metre programme, Kobo is advancing Kossou toward a maiden mineral resource estimate expected in H2 2026 while preparing for an inaugural drill campaign at the adjacent Kotobi Permit where previous surveys identified multiple large gold-in-soil anomalies across a prospective structural corridor.

headline: GLEASON (MONEY METALS): FORT KNOX GOLD IS IMPURE, UNAUDITED AND UNFIT FOR INTERNATIONAL TRADE — DE-DOLLARIZATION MAKES THE SHORTFALL A SECURITY RISK
snippet: In a June 24 Pinnacle Digest Podcast interview, Money Metals President and CEO Stefan Gleason argues that the U.S. gold reserve at Fort Knox consists largely of 99.5% pure bars that do not meet current 99.9% 'good delivery' standards for international settlement — and that government claims of audits represent paperwork reviews rather than physical counts, raising the possibility of a meaningful gap between the official 8,133-tonne reserve figure and what is actually tradeable. Gleason frames the controversy within the accelerating de-dollarization trend: the freezing of Russian assets in 2022 taught every sovereign nation that dollar-based reserves can be restricted, and the structural shift of central banks toward gold — buying above 1,000 tonnes annually for three consecutive years — reflects a durable non-inflationary bid under the metal that transcends short-term rate hike fears.

headline: "IT WAS NEVER THE WAR" — GOLD'S BEAR DRIVER IS THE RATE CHANNEL, NOT IRAN; THE PEACE DEAL REMOVES NOTHING THAT WAS REALLY THERE
snippet: A June 23 FXStreet analysis cuts through the Iran ceasefire narrative to argue that gold's 26% decline from January's $5,589 all-time high was driven by the rate channel and dollar strength — not geopolitical risk premium — meaning the Iran peace framework cannot rationally be blamed for the current selloff since 'a clean, durable peace was already priced and it never put a bid under the metal in the first place.' The piece notes that the Iran situation remains ambiguous: the Strait of Hormuz is still mined, the Iranian president insists the country will never abandon enrichment, nuclear talks in Switzerland were postponed, and fighting in Lebanon has not stopped — meaning the 'peace premium' markets are unwinding may be overstated — while the actual driver, the Fed rate channel, has markets pricing September hikes near 90% odds with Deutsche Bank and Bank of America both forecasting an early move.

headline: PALLADIUM HITS $1,202 AS PLATINUM FAILS $1,665 SUPPORT — DOLLAR TESTING MAJOR CHANNEL AS PGM COMPLEX RISKS ANOTHER LEG LOWER
snippet: Technical analyst Anna Radomska flagged June 24 that palladium fell to $1,202 per ounce — down 3.34% on the day and below its prior $1,234 downside target — while platinum failed to defend the June intraday low and now requires a close above $1,665 to avoid a test of the $1,600 area, with both PGMs at elevated risk if the U.S. dollar breaks out of its rising channel and confirms above the 101.39–101.59 resistance zone. For PGM-exposed junior miners, the double-bear configuration — structural EV headwinds reducing long-run catalytic converter demand in China's rapidly electrifying auto market, compounded by the macro risk-off triggered by hawkish Fed pricing — creates a near-term technical setup where 'trading below the June 12 bullish gap increases risk of another leg lower' in palladium specifically.
